verses.text: Do not sacrifice to the LORD your God an ox or a sheep that has any defect or flaw, because the LORD your God hates that.
Suppose a man or woman living in one of the towns the LORD your God gives you is found doing evil in the sight of the LORD your God by breaking his covenant.
Suppose they have gone and worshipped other gods and bowed down to them, or to the sun or the moon or the stars in the sky, which I have forbidden.
If you are told about this, or hear about it, look into it carefully. If it is true and it is proven that this hateful thing has been done in Israel,
then take the man or woman who has done this evil thing to your town gate, and stone that person to death.
A person may be put to death only on the word of two or three witnesses. No one may be put to death on the word of only one witness.
The witnesses must be the first to throw stones at the person, and then all the people must join in. You must get rid of this evil from among you.

Some cases that come before your local courts may be too hard for you to judge, such as cases of murder, of who has the right in a quarrel, or of injury. Then take them to the place the LORD your God will choose.
Go to the priests, who are Levites, and to the judge who is in office at that time. Ask them about the case, and they will give you their decision.
You must act on the decision they give you at the place the LORD will choose. Be careful to do everything they tell you.
Follow the teaching they give you and the decision they announce. Do not turn away from what they tell you, to the right or to the left.
Anyone who proudly refuses to listen to the priest who stands there serving the LORD your God, or to the judge, must be put to death. You must get rid of the evil from Israel.
Then all the people will hear about it and be afraid, and they will not act proudly again.
You will enter the land the LORD your God is giving you, take it over, and settle in it. Then you may say, "Let us set a king over us, like all the nations around us."
If so, be sure to make the king the one the LORD your God chooses. He must be one of your own people. Do not put a foreigner over you, someone who is not a fellow Israelite.
The king must not gather large numbers of horses for himself, or send people back to Egypt to get more horses, for the LORD has told you, "You must never go back that way again."
He must not take many wives, or his heart will be turned away from the LORD. And he must not gather large amounts of silver and gold for himself.
When he sits on his royal throne, he must write out for himself a copy of this law in a book, taken from the copy kept by the priests, who are Levites.
He must keep it with him and read it every day of his life, so that he learns to fear the LORD his God and carefully obeys all the words of this law and these rules.

Then he will not think he is better than his fellow Israelites, and he will not turn away from the commands to the right or to the left. Then he and his descendants will rule his kingdom in Israel for a long time.
